newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Occidental wins dispute with Colombian Indians.
newsitem.headline: Occidental wins dispute with Colombian Indians.

text.p: Occidental Petroleum Corp has won a dispute with a small indigenous community in northeast Colombia that had sought to prevent the multinational oil giant from exploring its land for crude, authorities said on Wednesday.

Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar said the Council of State, a body set up to resolve conflicts between Colombian citizens and the state, had overturned a high court ruling last month preventing Occidental from exploring lands long considered the property of U'wa Indians.

The previous ruling, handed down by the Constitutional Court on Feb. 3, was based on a finding that the government and Occidental had failed to ask the U'was for permission to explore their land. But the Council of State ruled by 14 to 7 that they had.
The ruling effectively reopens what industry sources have described as a potentially oil-rich corner of Boyaca province, near Colombia's northeast border with Venezuela, to exploration by Occidental.

Villamizar told national radio that exploration activity would remain on hold, however, pending a new round of talks between government officials, representatives of Occidental and leaders of the U'wa community.

Representatives of the U'was, who number no more than about 4,000 people nationwide, had threatened at a news conference in Bogota in late January to commit mass suicide if their lands were opened up to Occidental.
Spokesmen for Occidental could not be reached for immediate comment on the ruling announced by the Council of State on Tuesday night.
